3) EAST cluster was never QC'd at all — this spot-check covered South + North only. East QC is now tracked as its own issue and is outstanding.

Conclusion: my earlier sign-off does not hold and this cluster QC is NOT closeable. Set to In Progress pending (a) the North/South field items being worked and re-inspected (calendar hold set for 7/8) and (b) East QC being completed.

fields.Description: PM Push field follow-up — NORTH cluster. Two units flagged during my QC walkthrough on 5/23/2026 (Jaime Salinas) as needing a tech back onsite right away: HVAC coil service / refrigerant check, a plumbing item, and an electrical panel check per unit. These field flags were never captured in a tracking record until now. Needs an HVAC tech (John Smith, North) dispatched onsite; QC re-inspection to follow (calendar hold 7/8, ref OPS-87). Unit numbers to be confirmed on site.

PM Push field follow-up — SOUTH cluster no-access unit. Tenant was out during the scheduled HVAC service window (ref OPS-43); the unit never received its coil cleaning / refrigerant check / filter swap / condensate flush. Carlos Mendez to reschedule tenant access; Elias Navarro to service once access is set. QC re-inspection to follow. Blocks South cluster closeout.

PM Push field follow-up — PLUMBING (Carlos Mendez's cluster). Plumbing inspection on 5/31/2026 flagged two water heaters for replacement and several hose bibs needing repair. Water-heater replacements were approved as a budget priority (ref OPS-93 reconciliation) but field completion is unconfirmed. Needs a vendor/tech onsite to replace the two water heaters and repair the hose bibs. Owner: Carlos Mendez to schedule vendor. Owner-billable — start pass-through paperwork.

PM Push field follow-up — HVAC watch items (flagged by Elias Navarro, 5/20/2026). Two units with recurring condensate-drain clogs flagged for follow-up, plus one compressor to monitor heading into peak heat. Needs a tech to re-check the two drain lines and evaluate the compressor before the season peaks. Owner: Elias Navarro.

input.body:
Brooke,

Before I put my name to closing out the Preventive Maintenance Push, I went back through every piece of it — Linear, the maintenance log, and the channel history — and reconciled our records to what's actually true as of today. I've already corrected the tracking so it reads straight, raised items for everything still open with an owner on each, and put the field follow-ups into the maintenance log. Here's where it stands.

Up front, so there's no reading this two ways: my QC side is NOT a pass. My earlier sign-off does not hold, and the push should not be treated as closeable yet. The reasons are below, cluster by cluster.

FILTERS (portfolio-wide) — PASS
The filter-replacement spot-check was genuinely clean, no rework. That one holds. I've finalized it (OPS-96 → Done). It's the only QC line that closes cleanly.

NORTH CLUSTER — OPEN
- Two units I flagged on my 5/23 field walkthrough (coil, plumbing, electrical panel) still need a tech back onsite. Those were never captured in any tracking record until now — I've logged them as MT-2026-PMP-N1. Owner: John Smith to work them; me to re-inspect.
- North preventive inspections (coil cleanings, A/C checks, vendor walk-throughs) were never executed — OPS-44 sat in Backlog since 5/14. I've reassigned it to Lisa Smith (with John) and moved it to Todo.
- Before North can close: both flagged units repaired and re-inspected, and OPS-44 inspections completed.

SOUTH CLUSTER — OPEN
- One holdover: the no-access unit was never serviced (tenant out during the scheduled window). Logged as MT-2026-PMP-S1. Owner: Carlos Mendez to reschedule access, Elias Navarro to service once access is set.
- My South "pass" only ever covered a sample of completed units, so it never touched this unit.
- Before South can close: unit serviced and QC-inspected.

EAST CLUSTER — OPEN
- East was never confirmed complete (OPS-66 still reads "underway") and was never QC'd at all — my South/North spot-check did not cover it. I've moved OPS-66 back to In Progress. Owner: Elias Navarro to confirm East service is done.
- East QC is raised as its own item (OPS-1000), owned by me, blocked until service is confirmed.
- Before East can close: service confirmed complete, then East QC passed.

PLUMBING (Carlos's cluster) — OPEN
- The plumbing inspection flagged two water heaters for replacement and several hose bibs for repair. Budget was approved, but field completion is unconfirmed. Logged as MT-2026-PMP-PL1. Owner: Carlos Mendez to schedule the vendor; owner-billable, so pass-through paperwork should start.

HVAC WATCH — OPEN
- Elias's 5/20 flags — two recurring condensate-drain clogs and one compressor to watch into peak heat — are logged as MT-2026-PMP-HV1. Owner: Elias Navarro.

Why my sign-off doesn't hold, plainly:
1. My cluster QC (OPS-87) was run on a sample of completed units only — it could not and did not cover the South no-access unit or the two North units I myself flagged as deficient.
2. The two North deficiencies I flagged on 5/23 were never recorded on any tracking item, and OPS-87's own note claims cluster comments that don't actually exist. The paper trail was thinner than it read.
3. East was never QC'd.

So a genuine QC pass covers filters only. The three clusters each still have open field work and/or missing QC.

Next steps on my end: I've put a re-inspection on my calendar for 7/8 to go back out on the North and South field units and run the East QC once the upstream work is done. The push can close once (a) MT-2026-PMP-N1 and -S1 are worked and re-inspected, (b) OPS-44 North inspections are completed, (c) East service is confirmed and OPS-1000 East QC passes, and (d) the plumbing items (PMP-PL1) are completed. Happy to walk the whole list with you whenever works.

Thanks,
Jaime

|---|---|---|

| **South HVAC** | ❌ 1 holdover | No-access unit never serviced → **MT-2026-PMP-S1** (Carlos access, Elias service) |

| **Plumbing** | ❌ Open | 2 water heaters + hose bibs → **MT-2026-PMP-PL1** (Carlos, owner-billable) |

- **OPS-96** (filters) → **Done**, with a note it landed as a pass.

One judgment call worth flagging: I logged the plumbing and HVAC-watch items to the maintenance log and named their field owners even though they sit slightly outside my direct QC lane — they were flagged in the field, still need a tech, and would otherwise fall through the cracks at closeout.
